tools.name: find_mytools_tools
tools.description: Search the MyTools catalogue of free browser-based file tools for PDF, image, video and audio. Returns matching tools with their slug, page path and whether they can load files from a URL. Use this first to discover what MyTools can do, then call open_mytools_tool with the slug. Results are capped, so narrow the search with query, category or inputType rather than asking for everything at once.

query.description: Keywords to match against tool names and descriptions, e.g. 'rotate pdf'.

category.description: Restrict to one family of tools.

inputType.description: MIME type of the file to process, e.g. 'application/pdf' or 'image/jpeg'.

limit.description: Maximum number of tools to return. Default 8, maximum 10.

tools.name: open_mytools_tool
tools.description: Open a MyTools tool page so it is ready to use. Pass urls to load remote files straight into the tool and skip the upload step — only for tools that find_mytools_tools reports as byUrl. Opening a tool replaces the page-specific tools available to you, so read the tool list again afterwards. All file processing happens locally in the browser; nothing is uploaded to a server.

slug.description: Tool slug from find_mytools_tools, e.g. 'merge-pdf' or 'crop-image'.

urls.description: Optional http(s) URLs of files to load into the tool. Only for tools with byUrl: true.

carryResult.description: Hand the files the current tool just produced straight to the tool being opened, instead of arriving at an empty upload screen. Defaults to true whenever this page has a result and no urls were given. Set false to open the tool empty.

tools.name: suggest_mytools_pipeline
tools.description: Given a MyTools tool slug and the names of the files it just produced, list the tools those files can be passed to next. Use it to chain operations, for example crop-image then compress-image then jpg-to-pdf. Only compatible destinations are returned: a batch of files is never offered to a single-file tool, and no tool is offered a format it cannot open.

slug.description: Slug of the tool that produced the files, e.g. 'crop-image'.

fileNames.description: Names of the produced files, with extensions — the type is read from those.
